title: Harness of Minervini v2 ticker.chart response

exit_codes.0: A valid domain envelope was emitted; its status may still be partial, unavailable, or needs_input.
exit_codes.2: The request or arguments were invalid; stdout contains a needs_input error envelope.
exit_codes.3: An unexpected internal contract failure occurred; stdout contains an unavailable error envelope.

as_of.description: Completed US trading session in YYYY-MM-DD form; defaults to the latest completed regular session.

format.description: Output detail only; compact preserves verdict, signals, and missing evidence while omitting verbose basis rows.

no_cache.description: Bypass both provider-cache reads and writes for this invocation.

output_dir.description: Destination directory; defaults to the ignored .artifacts/charts directory.

limitations: Charts corroborate qualitative ambiguity but never override a deterministic hard gate. A history the measuring side will not read is refused here too rather than rendered: two definitions of a usable bar let a chart succeed off bars ticker.setup rejects, and the artifact then carried a null input digest -- the one thing a setup approval has to name.

Weekly is rendered before daily; historical as-of is enforced before rendering. A weekly bar is kept for the sessions it aggregates rather than for the Friday it is labelled with, so a week read mid-way through, or one whose Friday is a holiday, keeps its bar and its anchors instead of vanishing. Such a bar aggregates only the sessions it has, which makes its volume short for a reason that is not the stock going quiet, and the manifest flags it as last_bar_partial. Artifact paths carry the bars' own digest and the overlay's, so two renders of different history into one directory cannot interleave into a manifest that names one digest beside a picture drawn from another -- the digest is what a setup approval cites. The renderer's own version is in the name as well, because the digests say what went in and the name is claimed for what comes out: the same bars through two versions of this module are two different pictures, and one silently replacing the other left a manifest reporting a version the picture beside it was not drawn by. In the name rather than refused, so a version bump writes a new bundle instead of making every directory holding an older one unusable. Both digests in that name are truncated and so are shareable, so the name is claimed rather than assumed: a render whose name is already held by a different input or a different renderer refuses instead of drawing. The claim covering the render itself is a separate file, never the manifest, so nothing here can delete a finished one. It is also exclusive -- one render inside a name at a time, decided by the filesystem -- so a second render of the same name is refused while the first is drawing and told to retry once that one ends, which is all a refusal can honestly say: the render being waited on may be that same input, or a colliding vintage another directory settles, or one that fails and leaves nothing under the name at all. That costs a caller a retry and is what makes cleanup after a failure safe to reason about at all: with no claim standing and no finished manifest, nothing under the name was ever completed. A claim outliving the render that made it blocks only its own name and is safe to delete by hand once nothing is running. Publishing is the last thing that happens, and by then the name holds this render's pictures and no others: one left there by a render that was killed is cleared first, since a shareable name can be taken next by an overlay drawing a different set of panels and the stranded one would sit under these digests reported by nothing. Every path the manifest is about to name is asked for before it is written, because a manifest is read by somebody who opens what it names -- and a destination that stopped answering to the same directory mid-render splits the pictures across two of them.

The detector's turning points and its pivot are marked on the price panel, because this is where a person turns that proposal into the approval ticker.setup asks for. A segmentation the detector will not vouch for draws nothing rather than showing a structure the engine refuses to use. Each anchor is placed on the bar containing its session -- the session itself on the daily chart, the week it fell in on the weekly -- and one the chart does not reach is left off. Every manifest artifact lists the anchors its own picture contains, so what was drawn is not inferred from what was available.

The Power Play spans are drawn too, and they are the questions ticker.power-play raises from this history rather than a structure this capability picked out for itself. That capability cannot settle the volume clause alone -- the source says an explosive move commences on huge volume and names no number -- so it issues a chart question per undecided criterion per candidate top and waits, and each question carries the whole span it is about. Read here with nothing answered, because answers live in a request and this capability is not in it: the picture is what a reader is asked before they answer, and a span they have since settled is drawn again rather than dropped. The picture shows, for every open question, the anchor the advance is measured from, the peak it ended on, the flag low, the quiet window the volume ratio was divided by, and the heaviest session of the advance -- as far as the question named them. That anchor is the last quiet session and the advance is read from the one after it, so the rule is labelled as beginning the move after the session it stands on rather than on it: a session's difference lands on exactly the judgment a reader opens this picture to make. A history ending on the peak has no flag low and one beginning inside the advance has no baseline, and a landmark the question did not carry is not on the picture. Each artifact reports what it drew one list per landmark, so a mark that is absent because nothing named it is distinguishable from one absent because this timeframe does not reach the session. A chain read to several tops is usually one advance, so a landmark is drawn once per bar it falls on and carries the dates of every reading that landed there, only where the readings actually differ. Counted per bar rather than per date because a weekly bar holds a week of them: deduped by date, five tops drew five stars at three positions with five legend entries behind them. The key is on no picture and never will be, so the legend's date is all a reader has to carry a mark back to the question it belongs to -- and at five entries over three marks it carried nothing. A mark that stands for more than one reading sits where that bar's readings reached -- the highest of the tops, the lowest of the flag lows -- and prints no volume multiple where they divided by different baselines. Every value comes from the question, so the two cannot describe different tops with the same digest on both -- which is what happened when this capability measured its own: it drew the highest top while the question was about a lower one, and the seam accepted the answer. The ratio is printed only where the bars are sessions -- the daily panel and the span panel: it divides one session's volume by a session baseline, and a weekly bar is five of them added together, so the weekly marks which week holds that session and states no multiple. The baseline it divides by is that window's median, and the median is drawn across the shaded window on those same panels, because it is the one number on the panel a reader cannot point at: shown the shade alone, the eye compares the marked session with the tallest bar inside it, and on a quiet window holding one enormous day a session marked ten times the baseline is visibly shorter than a bar in the shade. The legend names the median rather than the window for the same reason. Where there is a span, a third picture holds it: the sessions from a week before the quiet window through the last bar, and no more -- the lead-in so that window's left edge is visible as an edge rather than as the side of the page. Three years of history is seven hundred sessions in twelve inches, and a four-session flag there is a few pixels under a marker wider than the flag -- a reader asked whether that flag corrected no more than a quarter was looking at something they could not measure. The two whole-history pictures are what a base is read from and are unchanged; this one is where the flag and the volume ratio are judged, and it draws no moving averages, because an average over one span is not the one the daily panel draws at the same dates. Nothing is drawn when nothing is being asked, and this capability holds no opinion about whether a structure deserves the question. The overlay names its own input beside itself, in power_play.measured_bars: input_sha256 covers the five price columns, which identifies the candles but not this overlay, since a split or a payout inside a span changes which questions exist without touching a price. Two histories differing only there once produced two questions and a chart with no span at all, digests matching on both, and the answer read off that blank picture was accepted. It is null where the history did not carry both kinds of event -- splits and distributions alike, since a payout inside a span withdraws criteria a split would leave undecided -- and a history missing either one is one no question is issued from.
x-capability-contract.output: Chart artifact paths plus an input-hash manifest recording ticker, as-of, timeframe order, completed-bar provenance, the swing segmentation drawn on the price panel, and a power_play block holding the spans drawn from ticker.power-play's open questions with the two digests they were drawn and measured from. Weekly and daily always; a third power_play picture as well wherever there is a span, holding those sessions with a week of lead-in and nothing else.
side_effects: Writes deterministic PNG artifacts and a manifest to the requested directory; the default directory is git-ignored. A claim file sits beside the manifest for the length of the render and is removed when it ends. A picture left under this render's name by an earlier one is deleted before the manifest is published. One left behind is a render that was killed, or one whose destination stopped taking changes before it could give the claim up -- giving it up is never allowed to fail a render whose files are all on disk, because a caller with an exception and no paths cannot find the bundle it just wrote. Either way it blocks that one name against every render, this same input included, until it is deleted -- any other ticker, date, input or renderer is untouched -- and deleting it by hand is safe once no render is running.

status_meanings.needs_input: The destination path or ticker is invalid, or the destination cannot hold artifacts -- a path that is a file, or under one, or one this process cannot write -- or another render is inside the name this one would take, which a retry settles once that one ends, or that directory already holds a finished bundle from a different render under it -- two inputs whose truncated digests met, which a different --output-dir settles -- or it stopped answering to the same directory partway through the render, which leaves part of the bundle where that path used to lead.
status_meanings.ok: The chart artifacts and the manifest were written -- weekly and daily, and the power_play picture as well wherever there is a span to hold.
status_meanings.partial: Completed price history stops before the requested session, so no artifact is written.
status_meanings.unavailable: Completed price history is unavailable, or the history the provider returned is not renderable -- the reason names which, in the same vocabulary ticker.swings uses, because a caller told only that something failed cannot tell a data problem from a bug.

x-capability-contract.summary: Render auditable weekly-first and daily chart artifacts, plus a span-only panel wherever there is Power Play structure to read, from the same completed bars used by deterministic analysis.
